newsitem.title: PERU: Pilots at Peru's Faucett airline halt flights.
newsitem.headline: Pilots at Peru's Faucett airline halt flights.

text.p: Pilots from the Peruvian domestic airline Faucett began a work stoppage Tuesday in protest at unpaid wages, forcing the company to cancel 14 national flights, airport authorities said.

"They owe us five months from last year and a month and a half from this year, notwithstanding the discounts from taxes," the president of the Faucett Pilots Association, Alberto Alvarez, told Reuters, insisting the action was a "paralyzation" rather than a strike.
Of Faucett's 55 planes, only two were being flown, he added.

"This is to protect the passenger. We cannot fly with the stress we have," said Alvarez. "Our kids do not go to college, ... the banks are pressuring us and there is no communication with the directors."
He added that the pilots would continue these measures until the situation was resolved.
